reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Counting cranial nerve palsy as a major focal deficit.
name: WFNS Subarachnoid Haemorrhage Grade

version.label: Original WFNS (1988)
version.detail: GCS with presence of major focal deficit. GCS 15 with a focal deficit is not defined in the original scale. The 2015 modified WFNS is a different scale.

purpose: Grading of aneurysmal SAH from GCS and focal motor deficit.

inputDefinitions.label: Major focal neurological deficit
inputDefinitions.help: Commonly interpreted as hemiparesis or aphasia.

resultStates.label: Not defined in original WFNS
resultStates.summary: The original WFNS does not define a grade for GCS 15 with a focal deficit.
resultStates.detail: Document GCS and the deficit explicitly.

resultStates.label: Grade IV
resultStates.summary: GCS 7–12. Commonly grouped as poor grade.
resultStates.detail: Assess for hydrocephalus, seizures and other reversible causes according to local protocol.

resultStates.label: Grade V
resultStates.summary: GCS 3–6. Commonly grouped as poor grade.
resultStates.detail: Assess for hydrocephalus, seizures and other reversible causes according to local protocol.

clinicalContext.text: A widely used SAH grade based on GCS.

clinicalInsights.text: In this GCS range the deficit separates Grade II from III.

confounders.effect: GCS may not be fully testable.

guideSections.what: A five-grade SAH scale from GCS and major focal deficit.
guideSections.howToPerform: 15 without deficit = I; 13–14 without = II; 13–14 with = III; 7–12 = IV; 3–6 = V.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Grades IV–V are commonly termed poor grade.

sources.citation: Drake CG. Report of World Federation of Neurological Surgeons Committee on a Universal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Grading Scale. J Neurosurg. 1988;68(6):985-986.
